evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: For 'Космический шутер', the learner can the complete, standalone final game (projects/pygame/space-shooter/space_shooter.py, 661 lines): 5 classes (Game/Player/Bullet/Enemy/Explosion), Vector2+dt movement, sprite-group collisions, lives+invulnerability, bounded difficulty scaling, explicit GameStatus state machine with full restart contract, procedural stars, original synthesized audio, and asset paths anchored to the file's own location.

asset paths built from Path(__file__).resolve().parent, not CWD -- confirmed: ran the game headlessly from CWD=/tmp (far from the repo) and it loaded all assets and ran correctly — no CWD-relative path bug

dt units are consistently seconds everywhere (clock.tick(FPS)/1000.0, then min()-clamped to MAX_DT=0.05 once in update(), and every velocity/timer multiplication uses that same dt) -- confirmed by full source read plus a 120-frame simulated run with no unit-mismatch symptoms (no teleporting, no frozen timers)
pygame.Vector2.normalize() on a zero vector raises ValueError, correctly guarded by length_squared()>0 in Player.move() -- confirmed directly under pygame-ce 2.5.8

collision detection is Rect-based (groupcollide/spritecollide, both operating on sprite.rect by default) — not pixel-perfect, and the chapter's prose never claims otherwise -- confirmed: no pixel-perfect claim anywhere in scripts/build_chapter_21.py

restart (start_new_game()) resets every piece of transient state (bullets/enemies/explosions/player/score/lives/spawn_timer/fire_cooldown/invulnerable_timer/stars) while preserving high_score -- confirmed by directly dirtying all of this state and calling start_new_game(): every field returned to its documented default, high_score preserved

no busy loops: run() paces via self.clock.tick(FPS) every iteration; update()'s internal while-loops (spawn timer, explosion frames) are bounded by positive constants unrelated to dt, so they always terminate -- confirmed via source read plus live execution; no unbounded spin observed across hundreds of simulated frames

EnemySpec is declared @dataclass(frozen=True), a dataclass feature never shown/explained anywhere in the chapter's 26 theory sections, and not formally taught until Chapter 23 (later in the curriculum) -- confirmed via grep across scripts/build_chapter_21.py (only mention of 'EnemySpec' is a bare exercise prompt in 21.25) and across scripts/build_chapter_*.py (grep 'frozen=True' hits only build_chapter_14.py: none, build_chapter_23.py: yes) — students following the chapter's own material never see this syntax explained

Game supports an F3 debug-overlay toggle (hitbox outlines in red + live FPS counter via _render_debug_overlay()) that is undocumented both in the module's own docstring ('Управление: ...' lists arrows/space/P/Enter/Esc but omits F3) and in the chapter's theory text (zero mentions of F3/debug overlay anywhere in build_chapter_21.py) -- confirmed: grep for 'F3' in space_shooter.py finds only the key-check itself, no docstring mention; grep for 'F3' in build_chapter_21.py finds nothing at all

Game.resolve_enemy_escapes() costs one life per escaped enemy, uncapped, bypassing invulnerability — behaves fundamentally differently from collision damage (which IS capped+invulnerability-protected, as taught in 21.16) -- confirmed by direct execution: 3 simultaneously 'escaped' enemies removed 3 lives (3->0) even while the player was invulnerable; this mechanic is undocumented anywhere in the chapter (see linked finding on 21-16)
dist/projects/pygame/space-shooter/space_shooter.py is byte-identical to the source copy -- confirmed via diff -- no drift between the published mirror and the source

all 5 image assets and all 3 audio assets referenced by AssetStore actually exist on disk with sane, non-corrupt content -- confirmed: PIL successfully opened and reported plausible dimensions for all 5 PNGs (all RGBA, dimensions consistent with the constants used in the historical-prototype sections); all 3 .wav files present
